entry_points: dependency_closure(seed_ids, edges, direction, max_depth, max_nodes, max_edges, authoritative_only, edge_kinds) -> dict
mandatory_semantic_closure(graph, decision_id, max_nodes, max_edges, max_depth) -> dict
deterministic_properties: dependency_closure normalizes nonempty seed IDs in lexical order, returns sorted node IDs and paths, and fail-closes invalid directions and invalid or overflowing bounds.

impact_from_index normalizes changed symbols and paths, returns sorted reverse impact and validation selection, and exposes unknown changes as uncovered impact rather than silently treating them as complete.
mandatory_semantic_closure sorts traversed edges, returns sorted node and edge IDs plus lexical shortest paths, and accepts only an authoritative decision seed and authoritative mandatory edges.
code_evidence_adapter.rejection_reason: These are bounded closure/impact selectors over a supplied canonical graph or index. mandatory_semantic_closure's complete=true means that its finite traversal completed within its graph and bounds; it is not a statement that a PCSM source forest or semantic slice is complete. None emits a versioned completeness witness, binds included/omitted source semantics to a forest source-map CID, or declares assumptions and expansion requirements.

limitations: This task is receipt-only: it assesses existing current-head controls without mutating proof_context or creating a competing completeness authority.
Bounded graph closure complete=true concerns only traversal of a supplied graph under finite bounds. It cannot be promoted into a source-forest completeness or semantic-equivalence assertion.
ContextPack source CIDs and freshness flags are caller-supplied context sufficiency inputs, not aggregate PCSM source-map/forest coverage or a completeness witness.
The authoritative sealed validation environment lacks anyio, so this receipt cannot promote completion despite the provider-side suite passing.
The receipt has no immutable self-CID because minting a self-describing CID would change its bytes.
